title: NotebookLM Pricing 2026: Free, Plus, Pro and Limits
summary: NotebookLM pricing is charged per seat, so costs scale with each team member you add. The Ultra plan exists but its price hasn't been published.
body_markdown:
## Feed NotebookLM weekly sources automatically with Activepieces


If the week's transcripts and PDFs arrive by email, Drive or a form, Activepieces can collect them into one folder on its free plan, which allows unlimited flows, so that your upload to NotebookLM is a single step. It doesn't raise any NotebookLM limit.


That distinction matters for the cap you're trying to confirm. A tidier intake changes how much hand-work goes into each upload, not how many sources, queries or notebooks the plan allows.


Activepieces is an MIT-licensed core automation platform with 774 integrations, and you build a flow there from a trigger followed by actions. Its connectors library groups those integrations by category, and the ones this job needs sit near the top of the popularity sort:


- Webhook for receiving a form submission
- Gmail for pulling attachments from a mailbox
- [Google Sheets](https://www.activepieces.com/pieces/google-sheets) for logging what arrived
- a generic HTTP integration for anything without its own connector


When an integration isn't in the library, you'll be wiring it by hand through HTTP, which makes the library page a useful first check. Once the integrations are chosen, the flow's short enough to describe in a line.


### What the NotebookLM source workflow does


The flow does three things. It watches a source, such as a shared inbox, a Drive folder or a form.


It copies each new transcript or PDF into one named folder. Optionally, it writes a row to a sheet so someone can see what came in this week.


It doesn't touch NotebookLM itself. Whether a source can be pushed into a notebook automatically depends on what NotebookLM's documentation supports today, and you should read that before building anything that assumes it.


If a Drive folder is a supported source type for your plan, the folder the flow fills can be added directly. If not, a person still does the final upload, and the flow has saved only the gathering.


Hold the cost question the same way.


A run of a flow costs 1 credit however many steps it has, and the free plan includes 1,000 credits a month, so count the runs a busy inbox would trigger against that before pointing it at the flow.


A team that already uploads by hand from one tidy folder can skip this section; the flow earns its place only when collecting files is the slow part.
